scope: Second quality pass for A3tal Egypt: Hyundai Elantra and MG6, with Tucson NX4 pass control
method: Manual evaluation from full live rendered article text; fact-specific checks versus factory Hyundai Egypt CN7 brochure and MG6 Egypt brochure. Quality percentages are editorial judgment, not Google scores, and length alone is not an editing trigger.

findings: Page wisely distinguishes Elantra generations, but provides no VIN-to-engine Egyptian model illustration or model-specific official supporting source.
No symptom-to-test measurement table or detailed differentiation of oil loss, cooling, fuel trims, misfire or urgent stop cases.
No inline explainer or verified links for genuine associated gearbox/airbag diagnostics; current page would not answer a practical repair decision.
Correct in principle that 6AT and IVT differ, but fails to verify Egypt CN7 1.6 MPI 6-speed AT official Hyundai brochure and leaves confusion for shoppers.
No owner decision matrix for hot delayed engagement versus engine misfire, speed-dependent bearing whine, voltage and TCM events.
Does not specify which fluid and code checks prevent destructive IVT vs 6AT mistakes; no OEM source or inline diagram.
Useful caution not to assume wet/dry DCT, but no reference link to Egyptian 2023 MG6 brochure for seven-speed dual clutch and version applicability.
Needs separate actual DCT low-speed creep and clutch heat symptoms from engine misfire and voltage errors, with service-protocol safeguards.
No table, flow image or related model links to MG6 infotainment and engine guides.
Already has approx 2166 words in rendered article, factory Hyundai owners manual citation, codes grouped with symptom-specific fault isolation, original image and diagnostic table.
No critical in-scope factual defect observed in initial manual sampling; leave unchanged despite previous short-source inventory.
